neighbours.label: the word ' too' meaning 'also' at the end of a clause
fire: My brother wanted to come along too, so we waited for him.
She speaks French and German too, which helped on the trip.
If you like the soup, try the bread too before it is gone.
The dog was hungry, and the cat was hungry too that night.
We visited Rome and stopped in Florence too on the way back.
He fixed the sink and painted the kitchen too last weekend.
Bring your sister too if she is free on Saturday.
The teacher praised the essay and the drawings too in class.
quiet: My brother wanted to come along as well, so we waited for him.
She speaks French and German fluently, which helped on the trip.
If you like the soup, try the bread before it is gone.
The dog was hungry, and the cat was also hungry that night.
We visited Rome and stopped in Florence on the way back.
He fixed the sink and painted the kitchen last weekend.
Bring your sister along if she is free on Saturday.
The teacher praised the essay and the drawings in class.

notes: top peaks are mixed (' too' x4, ' (' x2, ' one' x2); logit effect promotes ' too', ' also'
